destination.name: Botswana
destination.pitch: The most expensive destination in this catalogue by a wide margin, and the only one where the water arrives in the dry season, which is exactly what you are paying for.

because.nature: A 15,000 square kilometre inland delta that floods in the middle of the dry season, pushed by rain that fell in Angola four months earlier, with elephant density on the Chobe riverfront that has no equal anywhere.
because.exploration: Four unrelated landscapes inside one ten day loop: permanent swamp, seasonal floodplain, riverfront woodland and a salt pan the size of Switzerland where the horizon curves.
because.food: Camp food is competent set-menu lodge cooking and Maun has perhaps six restaurants worth the drive, so do not come here to eat.
because.relaxation: Three nights on a Delta island with no road in, no phone signal and a mokoro instead of a vehicle is as close to a full stop as safari gets.
because.culture: Bayei and Hambukushu poling knowledge in the Delta and Zu/'hoasi tracking in the Makgadikgadi are both here, and both are best met through the community trusts and the Kalahari camps rather than as a roadside stop.
because.adventure: Walking safaris on Chief's Island, night drives in the Khwai community area and a quad bike run out onto a dry pan at dusk, none of which are legal inside the national parks.
because.city: Maun is a supply town with an airport and a river through it, and one day there is one day too many.

destination.caveat: Botswana sells low volume at high price on purpose, so inner Delta camps run USD 500 to 3,000 per person per night with two or three night minimums, and every hop between them is a light aircraft with a 20 kg soft bag limit that eats half a day at each end. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: the Chobe riverfront
cities.base: Kasane, on the river side of the main road between Sedudu Gate and the Kazungula turn. Chobe Safari Lodge and Chobe Marina Lodge both have their own jetties, which saves you the transfer to the public

cities.base: The Ntwetwe Pan edge south of Gweta, where Jack's Camp, San Camp and Camp Kalahari sit in the same palm island cluster and run the meerkats, the quad bikes and the Kubu crossing between them. Planet B

outings.name: a mokoro morning on the Boro
outings.why: An hour of 4x4 to the buffalo fence crossing on the Boro, then two poles and two of you in a fibreglass mokoro for three hours, with a walk on an island in the middle. You see reeds, frogs, lechwe and possibly elephant at distance. It is no
outings.season: Full water May to September, thinning from October, and by D
outings.fallback: The Thamalakane channels at Matlapaneng, which can be poled in a short year but have no Delta game around them.

outings.name: a walking safari on Chief's Island
outings.why: Mokoro across to the island at first light, then three hours on foot with an armed guide, mostly tracking and reading dung rather than seeing big animals. The risk is real and the guide will make you walk single file and shut up.
outings.season: All year, best June to October when the island is dry underf
outings.fallback: A short poling loop in the channels behind camp, which still gets you the frogs and the birds without the walk.

outings.name: the Xakanaxa lagoon boat to the Gcodikwe heronry
outings.why: Aluminium boat out through the papyrus to a breeding colony of yellow-billed storks, marabou, herons and darters packed into one stand of trees. The noise and the smell are both considerable. Outside the breeding months it is an empty islan
outings.season: Colony active roughly August to November, water level permit
outings.fallback: The Xakanaxa channels and Dombo hippo pool, which hold birds and hippo all year.

outings.name: the Mboma Island sand ridge loop
outings.why: A 27 km sand track around an island of open grassland west of Third Bridge, good for cheetah, roan and big herds of tsessebe. The sand is deep, the drive is slow and you will not do it in under four hours.
outings.season: May to October; the loop is often closed or impassable Janua
outings.fallback: The Paradise Pools and Dead Tree Island circuit east of Third Bridge, shorter and firmer underfoot.

outings.name: the Khwai River night drive
outings.why: Out at 16:00, sundowner on the floodplain, then two hours under a red filter spotlight looking for leopard, genet, civet, porcupine and spring hare. Legal here in the community area and flatly illegal across the river in Moremi.
outings.fallback: An afternoon drive to the pole bridge and back before the gate hour, which still gets you elephant crossing at dusk.

outings.name: the Khwai pole bridge and the eastern floodplain
outings.why: The log bridge at Khwai is the classic elephant crossing and the drive east along the north bank is the best wild dog country in northern Botswana. Dogs are a coin flip on any given day; the elephants are not.
outings.season: All year, dogs denning roughly June to August
outings.fallback: The stretch of river immediately below the bridge, where hippo and saddle-billed stork sit whatever the roads are doing.

outings.name: the Chobe riverfront sunset cruise

startsFrom.name: Chobe Game Lodge, inside the park

outings.why: Three hours upstream from Kasane along the floodplain while several hundred elephant come down to drink and cross to the Namibian islands. The big shared double-deckers are loud; a small boat costs more and is worth it.
outings.season: All year, elephant concentrations highest August to November
outings.fallback: The short river loop from the lodge jetty at Kasane, which still reaches the first hippo pods.

outings.name: the Serondela morning drive on the Chobe riverfront

startsFrom.name: Chobe Game Lodge, inside the park

outings.why: Through Sedudu Gate at 06:00 and west along the river track past Puku Flats to the old Serondela sawmill site. Lion on the floodplain at dawn is common. So are twenty other vehicles by eight o'clock.
outings.season: All year; the river track is cut by water in some years arou
outings.fallback: The Ngoma road on the escarpment above the floodplain, drivable when the low track is under water.

outings.name: first light on Ntwetwe Pan
outings.why: Quad bikes out across the crust before dawn to a point with nothing in any direction, then breakfast on the salt. The flatness genuinely disorients people and the sun comes up very fast. Cold enough at 05:30 in July to need gloves.
outings.season: Dry pan only, roughly May to early November; the surface is
outings.fallback: The grass plain and palm islands on the pan edge, which stay drivable and hold the brown hyena and the springbok.

outings.name: the meerkat morning at Camp Kalahari
outings.why: A habituated wild colony that will stand on your head to get a better sightline once the sun warms them up. It is the least wild thing you will do in Botswana and also the one everybody remembers.
outings.season: All year, best May to September when the colony emerges late
outings.fallback: The Zu/'hoasi walk from camp, which covers the same ground on foot looking at plants and traps instead.

outings.name: Kubu Island and back across Sowa
outings.why: A granite outcrop covered in baobabs standing on the floor of Sowa Pan, with a stone wall on it nobody has fully explained. Getting there is four hours of pan and sand each way and the day is mostly driving.
outings.season: May to October only; the pan surface is impassable and the r
outings.fallback: Green's Baobab and the fallen trunk of Chapman's, both on the Gweta side and reachable in half a day.

outings.name: the Nxai Pan waterhole and Baines' Baobabs
outings.why: A fossil grassland pan north of the tar with a pumped waterhole that holds elephant and lion in the dry, plus the cluster of baobabs Thomas Baines painted in 1862, which are still recognisably the same trees. The 35 km of deep sand in from
outings.season: Baobabs all year; the pan itself is far better December to A
outings.fallback: Baines' Baobabs alone, 17 km off the main track and doable as a half day.

outings.name: the scenic flight over the permanent swamp
outings.why: Forty-five minutes at 150 metres in a Cessna 206 over the channels, the palm islands and the hippo trails, which is the only way to understand the shape of the place. Bumpy after ten in the morning and not for weak stomachs.
outings.season: All year, best June to August at peak flood
outings.fallback: The Delta leg of your scheduled camp transfer, which crosses the same water for free if you ask for a window seat.

places.name: The Old Bridge Backpackers
places.note: A thatched bar on a deck over a Thamalakane hippo pool, where every guide, pilot and poler in town ends up on a Friday. The food is burgers and stew and the point is the company.

places.name: Hilary's
places.neighborhood: Maun town centre, off Mathiba I Street
places.note: A small courtyard kitchen doing baked potatoes, sandwiches and a daily special, and the only decent coffee within walking distance of the government offices.

places.name: Marc's Eatery
places.note: International menu, competent salads and cakes, and a deli counter that will make up a packed lunch in half an hour if you are driving out to Moremi.

places.name: Tshilli Farmstall
places.note: Farm shop and coffee bar under trees with smashed avocado on sourdough and occasional live music, which in Maun counts as an event.

places.name: Motsana Centre and the Arts Cafe
places.note: A craft and performance yard with a kitchen doing Botswana and international fusion, and the best place in town to buy basketry without being ripped off.

places.name: Okavango River Lodge bar
places.note: Pub food in large portions on a riverbank terrace 10 km out of town, quieter than the Old Bridge and with the same hippo grunting at you after dark.

places.name: Sedia Riverside Hotel bar
places.note: An unglamorous poolside bar that stays open late and is where overland crews drink, which makes it a good place to find out which roads are actually open.

places.name: Nhabe Museum
places.note: One room of Ngamiland history and local painting in a 1939 colonial building, worth 40 minutes and no more, and it is where you learn who the Bayei and Hambukushu polers actually are.

places.name: Maun Airport charter terminal
places.note: The busiest light aircraft terminal in southern Africa and the hinge of your whole trip: soft bag only, 20 kg including hand luggage, and they will weigh you as well as the bag.

places.name: Ngami Centre supermarket
places.note: The last full supermarket before the Delta or the pans, and the place to buy the cash you will need, because most camps and gates do not take cards.

places.name: the Boro poling station
places.note: An hour of sand track from Maun to a clearing on the Boro where the mokoro trips start and the community trust rotates the polers. Water levels here decide everything and by December there may not be enough to float.

places.name: the old bridge over the Thamalakane
places.note: A short walk on the bank by the disused bridge for which the backpackers is named, good at dusk for carmine bee-eaters and the light going orange off the water.

places.name: Ntswi Island
places.neighborhood: Inner Delta, east of Chief's Island
places.note: The palm and fig island the water camps share, big enough to walk across in an hour and surrounded by channels deep enough to pole all year in a normal flood.

places.name: Chief's Island
places.note: The largest island in the Delta, 70 km long, and the only place most visitors will walk with an armed guide rather than ride. Buffalo and elephant make it genuinely dangerous, which is the point.

places.name: the Boro Channel
places.note: The main southern artery and the channel almost every Maun mokoro trip actually uses, lined with papyrus and day water lilies that shut by mid afternoon.

places.name: the Santantadibe Channel
places.note: The quieter eastern channel running down toward the Gomoti, less poled than the Boro and better for sitatunga if you are out at first light.

places.name: Gunn's Camp deck
places.note: A raised deck looking across the floodplain to Chief's Island, where the drinks are included in a rate you have already paid and the elephants cross in front of you at dusk.

places.name: Moremi Crossing
places.note: Meru tents with plumbing and a plunge pool, running roughly USD 480 to 580 per person per night including activities, which is the sensible middle of the inner Delta market.

places.name: Oddballs Camp
places.note: Dome tents on platforms with shared bathrooms and an unapologetic focus on mokoro and walking, from about USD 430 per person per night, and the cheapest honest way into the inner Delta.

places.name: Delta Camp
places.note: Solar powered, no motorboats and no vehicles at all, so everything is poled or walked. That is either the reason you came or the reason you should stay elsewhere.

places.name: the hippo trails through the reeds
places.note: The channels are kept open by hippo walking them, which is why a mokoro route can close overnight and why polers give a submerged pod a very wide berth.

places.name: Mombo Camp
places.note: The most famous camp in Botswana and around USD 3,000 per person per night in high season, with predator density to match. Skip it unless money is genuinely not the constraint.

places.name: the fire pit after dinner
places.note: No generator after ten, no phone signal, and a sky with the Magellanic Clouds visible to the naked eye. This is the part of the Delta nobody photographs and everyone remembers.

places.name: Xakanaxa Lagoon
places.note: The one place in Moremi where you can put a boat on permanent water and drive a vehicle from the same camp, which is why the lagoon cluster is worth the extra transfer.

places.name: the Gcodikwe heronry
places.note: A single stand of trees holding thousands of nesting storks, herons and darters in the late dry season, and an empty island the rest of the year. Check the colony is active before you commit a morning.

places.name: Third Bridge
places.note: A log causeway over a channel that has been rebuilt more times than anyone counts, famous for crocodiles under it and for the sign telling you not to swim, which people ignore and occasionally die for.

places.name: the Mboma Island sand ridge loop
places.note: Twenty-seven kilometres of deep sand around an island of open grassland, the best cheetah and roan ground in the reserve, and slow enough that half a tank disappears into it.

places.name: Dead Tree Island
places.note: A stand of drowned leadwoods on a floodplain that photographs better at dawn than anything else in Moremi, and holds nothing at all in the middle of the day.

places.name: Paradise Pools
places.note: A chain of clear pools on the Xakanaxa circuit that concentrate game as the floodplain dries, and the loop that stays drivable when the Mboma sand defeats you.

places.name: Dombo hippo pool
places.note: A permanent pool with a marked viewing point where you are allowed out of the vehicle, one of very few such spots in the reserve, and the hippos are loud about it.

places.name: Moremi South Gate
places.note: Where you pay the DWNP fee and sign in, roughly P270 per person per day for non-residents plus a vehicle fee, cash in pula, and there is nothing else here.

places.name: Camp Xakanaxa dining deck
places.note: Set menu lodge cooking on a deck over the lagoon, included in the rate, and the standard is decent rather than interesting. Nobody comes to Moremi for the food.

places.name: Fourth Bridge
places.note: Quieter than Third Bridge and usually the one that decides whether the Mboma loop is on, since it floods first and closes without warning.

places.name: Black Pools
places.note: Dark peat-stained water on the eastern circuit that draws elephant in late afternoon, and one of the few places in Moremi you can sit still for an hour and be rewarded.

places.name: the Khwai pole bridge
places.note: A bridge of tied logs over the Khwai that every vehicle in the area has to cross, and the best elephant crossing point in northern Botswana at about five in the afternoon.

places.name: Khwai village
places.note: A community of a few hundred people who hold the concession and run the campsites, with a craft stall or two. Ask before photographing anyone, and expect to be told no sometimes.

places.name: Moremi North Gate
places.note: The reserve gate on the south side of the river, where the Moremi fees and rules start and night drives stop being legal. Cash in pula, no card machine to speak of.

places.name: the Khwai River hippo pools
places.note: Permanent water immediately downstream of the bridge holding hippo, saddle-billed stork and a resident crocodile, and reliable on days when the floodplain drives come up empty.

places.name: Magotho campsite
places.note: A community campsite strung along the river east of the village with no fence and no facilities to speak of, and the reason people who have done this before still camp in Khwai.

places.name: Machaba Camp riverfront
places.note: Canvas tents facing the floodplain in an old-style camp layout, around USD 600 to 800 per person per night including activities, and the game walks past the tents most evenings.

places.name: Sango Safari Camp
places.note: One of the more affordable permanent camps on the river at roughly USD 450 to 550 per person per night, small, unfussy and well guided.

places.name: Sable Alley
places.note: A private reserve camp on a lagoon south west of the village, with boating in a good flood year, which the community area itself rarely offers.

places.name: Hyena Pan
places.note: A pumped pan with a sunken hide at water level, the one place around Khwai where you are eye to eye with drinking elephant rather than above them.

places.name: the eastern floodplain wild dog country
places.note: Open mopane and floodplain east of Magotho where the local pack dens in the winter months. Dogs are a coin flip on any given morning and the guides will not pretend otherwise.

places.name: the Khwai bush walk
places.note: Two and a half hours on foot with an armed guide, legal here and not in the reserve, and mostly about tracks, trees and birds rather than closing on big animals.

places.name: Sedudu Gate
places.note: The main park entrance five minutes from Kasane, where you pay the DWNP day fee and where the queue at 06:00 in August is genuinely long.

places.name: Serondela
places.note: The old sawmill site and picnic ground on the river, abandoned since the 1960s, now the turnaround point for most morning drives and a good spot to get out and stretch legally.

places.name: Puku Flats
places.note: Open floodplain a few kilometres in from the gate holding one of the only puku populations in Botswana, plus lion on the short grass at first light.

places.name: Ihaha campsite
places.note: The public campsite on the river inside the park, unfenced, with a long history of lion and hyena walking through it, which the ablution block wiring reflects.

places.name: Sedudu Island
places.note: The island the International Court of Justice awarded to Botswana over Namibia in 1999, now mostly a buffalo and elephant grazing flat that your cruise boat will circle.

places.name: Chobe Game Lodge
places.note: The only lodge inside the national park, with electric game vehicles and boats and an all-female guiding team, at roughly USD 700 to 900 per person per night.

places.name: Sedudu Bar and Grill, Chobe Safari Lodge
places.note: A big riverside terrace bar and grill at the main Kasane lodge, busy, unsubtle, and the most reliable cold beer in town with the river in front of it.

places.name: The Old House
places.note: A guesthouse restaurant in town doing steaks, curries and pizza in a garden, and the place locals suggest when you ask where to eat away from the lodges.

places.name: Thebe River Safaris bar
places.note: Campsite bar on the river where the overland trucks stop, cheaper than the lodges, and the noticeboard is the best source of same-day cruise and transfer prices.

places.name: the Kazungula Bridge
places.note: The 923 metre road and rail bridge opened in 2021 that replaced the ferry at the four-country river junction, and the reason the truck queues here are shorter than they used to be.

places.name: the Chobe Princess houseboats
places.note: Small houseboats that moor on the river for two or three nights, which swaps the vehicle entirely for water and is the best version of Chobe if you do not mind the pace.

places.name: Ntwetwe Pan
places.note: A dry salt pan roughly 100 km across with no vegetation and no reference points, where the curvature of the earth is visible on the horizon and a compass is not optional.

places.name: Kubu Island
places.note: A granite outcrop covered in baobabs standing on the floor of Sowa Pan, with an unexplained stone wall and Stone Age tools on the ground. Four hours of driving each way from the Ntwetwe camps.

places.name: Jack's Camp
places.note: Green canvas tents full of Persian rugs and natural history specimens, around USD 2,000 to 2,800 per person per night, and the camp that invented this whole style of Kalahari safari.

places.name: San Camp
places.note: White tents on the bare pan edge, open in the dry season only, and the most visually severe place to sleep in Botswana. No pool, no shade, deliberately.

places.name: Camp Kalahari
places.note: The least expensive of the three sister camps at roughly USD 700 to 900 per person per night, sharing the same guides, quad bikes and meerkats as the other two.

places.name: the meerkat colony
places.note: A habituated wild colony that treats standing humans as lookout posts once the morning warms up. Entirely wild, entirely unbothered by you, and the one thing everyone photographs.

places.name: the quad bike run onto the pan
places.note: Bikes out across the crust before dawn to a point with nothing in any direction. Dry season only, and it is properly cold at 05:30 between May and August.

places.name: Chapman's Baobab
places.note: A seven-trunked baobab used as a post office and a navigation mark by Livingstone and Selous, which collapsed in January 2016. The fallen trunks are still there and still worth the stop.

places.name: Green's Baobab
places.note: A standing baobab carved with nineteenth century traders' names including the Green brothers, and the honest alternative to Chapman's now that Chapman's is on the ground.

places.name: the Nxai Pan waterhole
places.note: A pumped waterhole on a fossil grassland pan north of the tar that holds elephant, lion and springbok, and fills with zebra from December to April when the rest of the country is at its worst.

places.name: Baines' Baobabs
places.note: The cluster of baobabs Thomas Baines painted in 1862, still recognisably the same trees on the same pan edge, and 17 km of sand track off the main Nxai route.

places.name: Planet Baobab, Gweta
places.note: Painted Kalahari huts, a pool and an aardvark bar on the tar road at Gweta village, at a fraction of the pan camp rates, and the last reliable diesel and bottle store before the pans.
